title: ChainGPT: Dual-Reasoning Model with Recurrent Depth and Multi-Rank State Updates
claim: A model block stacks a state-update layer and a sparse-attention layer, with states propagating sequentially and a few global anchors giving efficient long-range access.
layout: Left layer stacks zoomed into right token-column diagram; legend at far right
description: The figure has two parts. On the left, two rounded blue boxes are stacked and labeled Attention Layer (top) and State Layer (bottom). Each holds colored blocks with residual connections: yellow MLP and SGSA in the attention layer, yellow RWKV-Product in the state layer, and pink Norm blocks in both. Dashed gray lines expand these layers into the diagram on the right. That diagram has three rows of boxed tokens. The bottom row is x1–x9, the middle row is y1–y9 with black arrows between neighbors for state propagation, and the top row is s1–s9. Vertical lines connect the rows. In the top row, s3, s6 and s9 are shaded blue as global anchors. s8 has a red outline as the query position. Orange solid curves show the causal local window, and blue dashed curves show causal global anchors. A legend on the right explains the line and box styles.
caption: Chain-Block
abstract: Large language models, constrained by the fixed-depth Transformer architecture, struggle to solve complex reasoning tasks in an end-to-end manner. Existing approaches, such as Chain of Thought, improve reasoning depth to some extent but rely heavily on natural language generation, with computational costs increasing rapidly as the length of the generated sequence grows. To address these limitations, we propose ChainGPT, a dual-reasoning model that shifts reasoning into latent computational space. Within each layer, ChainGPT employs multi-substep state updates combined with state-guided sparse attention, enabling deep local computation and efficient long-range modeling without quadratic costs. Across layers, recurrent depth approach iteratively refine latent states, supported by adaptive training and stopping strategies that balance reasoning depth against computational budget. Theoretically, we show that ChainGPT can, in principle, simulate general computation, and empirically it delivers consistent improvements over comparable models, including on reasoning tasks that remain challenging for existing systems. By unifying efficiency and reasoning ability, ChainGPT provides a principled foundation for next-generation language models.
